core_themes.name: Growth and significance of the private rented sector
core_themes.claim: The private rented sector has grown substantially, making the scale and impact of letting agent fees on tenants a matter of national housing policy importance.

core_themes.name: High, variable and opaque tenant fees
core_themes.claim: Letting agents charge tenants fees that vary considerably in amount, structure and transparency, making them hard to understand, itemise or compare across agents.

core_themes.name: Asymmetric market power between landlords and tenants
core_themes.claim: Because landlords, not tenants, choose and can negotiate with letting agents, there is little competitive pressure to keep tenant-facing fees low, even where transparency rules are followed.

core_themes.name: Financial and behavioural harm to tenants
core_themes.claim: Repeated, high upfront fees create real financial hardship for tenants, deterring moves, exacerbating vulnerability, and potentially encouraging discriminatory practices.

core_themes.name: Ban chosen over continued transparency regulation
core_themes.claim: Because existing transparency requirements have not fixed the underlying market failure of weak tenant-side competition, the government has chosen an outright ban on tenant-paid letting fees rather than further transparency measures.

core_themes.name: Scope and design of the ban
core_themes.claim: The ban will cover all letting agent fees to tenants from agents, landlords or third parties, leaving only rent and a refundable deposit chargeable, in order to be clear and simple while protecting landlords and agents from undue risk.

core_themes.name: Scottish precedent as supporting evidence
core_themes.claim: Evidence from Scotland's long-standing ban on letting fees shows that similar bans can operate with minimal negative effects on the sector and only limited impact on rents, supporting the case for introducing a comparable ban in England.

core_themes.name: Expected market effects of the ban
core_themes.claim: The ban is expected to sharpen competition among agents for landlords' business, lower overall fee levels, and may lead to some pass-through into rents, but with net benefits for tenants' ability to compare and afford properties.

core_themes.name: Enforcement through local authorities, possibly a lead authority
core_themes.claim: The ban will be enforced primarily by local authority Trading Standards, building on their existing role, with the possible addition of a lead enforcement authority modelled on the Estate Agent sector to improve consistency.

core_themes.name: Permitted exceptions and deposit arrangements
core_themes.claim: To make the ban workable, certain charges—holding deposits and in-tenancy charges arising from tenant actions—will remain permitted, alongside measures to ease the burden of upfront deposits on tenants.

core_themes.name: Penalties and deterrence for non-compliance
core_themes.claim: Non-compliance with the ban will be deterred through civil penalties, potentially at a higher level than existing fines, with the option of criminal prosecution and banning orders for persistent offenders.

core_themes.name: Tenant empowerment and education to support compliance
core_themes.claim: Educating and empowering tenants to recognise and challenge unlawful fees, alongside improved data sharing across regulators, will reduce the enforcement burden on local authorities and improve compliance with the ban.
